cells.scene: A capable handyman repairs a loose cabinet hinge with a screwdriver, neat toolbox nearby and confident practical posture.
An adult creatively uses a fallen sturdy branch as a walking support after a walking-stick breaks, solved practical problem.
An adult admiring themselves as a champion carpenter in a thought bubble actually stands beside a crooked broken chair they made.
An adult carefully takes apart an unplugged old alarm clock, gears and casing laid out neatly on a workbench.

prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Create ONE SQUARE 2x2 atlas with four equal square cells for an adult vocabulary app. Attached image is STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: restrained ink-and-watercolor educational illustrations, clear dark blue-charcoal outlines, pale blue wash, small warm natural color accents. Pure WHITE opaque background. Central 75% of each quadrant contains its subject with generous margins. Nothing crosses midlines. Leave horizontal 45–55% and vertical 47–53% center bands EMPTY WHITE. Natural human anatomy, recognizable objects, clear 320px silhouettes, restrained detail, no elaborate environment. NO captions, labels, writing, borders, grid lines, watermarks or logos. Only symbols or numerals explicitly requested in a cell are allowed. Meanings are guidance; never write them. Row-major fixed order. CRITICAL SAFE COMPOSITION: Make the subjects SMALLER than the reference. Every subject fits within central 65% of its own quadrant, with a large 20% white margin on all sides. Bottom-row subjects including heads and thought bubbles begin BELOW 58% of the entire canvas height; top subjects end ABOVE 42%. Keep central horizontal 42–58% totally blank white. No piece, head or bubble crosses either exact 50% midline. FOUR CELLS:
TOP LEFT — handyman (n.手巧的人，能工巧匠): A capable handyman repairs a loose cabinet hinge with a screwdriver, neat toolbox nearby and confident practical posture.
TOP RIGHT — resourceful (a.足智多谋的): An adult creatively uses a fallen sturdy branch as a walking support after a walking-stick breaks, solved practical problem.
BOTTOM LEFT — delusion (n.错觉): An adult admiring themselves as a champion carpenter in a thought bubble actually stands beside a crooked broken chair they made.
BOTTOM RIGHT — dismantle (v.拆卸): An adult carefully takes apart an unplugged old alarm clock, gears and casing laid out neatly on a workbench.
review_notes: All four repaired cells visually checked: handyman repairs hinge; resourceful hiker uses branch after broken pole; imagined prize-winning skill contrasts broken chair; clock is dismantled into separate parts. Smaller composition now fully contains every head, thought bubble and tool within its exact quadrant.
